rf.RF-01.action: Request a demo video (including failed takes), BOM, and test records
rf.RF-01.name: Only papers or a proof-of-concept demo; no working unit or engineering prototype
rf.RF-02.action: Request the closed-loop link diagram and evidence of the feedback implementation; check against each of the four classification characteristics
rf.RF-02.name: One-way recording or one-way stimulation presented externally as a brain-computer interface
rf.RF-03.action: Send a formal evidence request against the checklist with a 10-business-day deadline
rf.RF-03.name: All evidence is company self-report (deck / roadshow); no third-party material
rf.RF-04.action: Move to the valuation-basis check; test the implied multiple against its band
rf.RF-04.name: Valuation basis visibly mismatched to asset class already at the gate stage
rf.RF-05.action: Record the refusal and its date, log it as an observation, and note it in evidence-collection status
rf.RF-05.name: Refuses to provide a prototype or refuses an on-site demo
rf.RF-06.action: Require the revenue line that matches the narrative and recompute the implied multiple on consumer logic
rf.RF-06.name: Consumer- or research-grade asset with zero or minimal revenue priced on a hard-tech option narrative
rf.RF-07.action: Verify the closed-loop link, revalue as monitoring equipment, and re-sequence exit expectations
rf.RF-07.name: Open-loop one-way monitoring product valued as a BCI platform
rf.RF-08.action: Split revenue and gross margin by product line; assess unit economics of the frontier line separately
rf.RF-08.name: Over 70% of revenue from a legacy business unrelated to the narrative, while only the frontier line is pitched
rf.RF-09.action: Require same-source, same-definition data and an explicit statement of where the BCI boundary is drawn
rf.RF-09.name: Market size quoted from several sources with inconsistent definitions, taking only the highest
rf.RF-10.action: List existing alternatives and compare gain against risk item by item
rf.RF-10.name: Risk-benefit inversion: the functional gain of a highly invasive approach is replaceable by lower-risk options
rf.RF-11.action: Provide independent interview records from at least five unrelated clinical experts
rf.RF-11.name: Need asserted by the technology itself; no independent clinical-need evidence
rf.RF-12.action: Verify the payment pathway for this indication and the payable amount per case
rf.RF-12.name: Single indication with no payer (no coverage, no ability to self-pay)
rf.RF-13.action: Require an online real-time demo and cross-day, cross-subject generalisation data
rf.RF-13.name: Only offline public-dataset cross-validation; no online real-time closed-loop validation
rf.RF-14.action: Require the control result with EMG / EOG channels disabled and a physical-feasibility explanation
rf.RF-14.name: Claims non-invasive EEG decoding of complex semantics, dozens of characters, or full thoughts
rf.RF-15.action: Identify the specific feedback implementation and its latency metrics
rf.RF-15.name: No closed-loop feedback; one-way monitoring presented as BCI
rf.RF-16.action: Require an ablation: how far performance falls when the neural input is disconnected
rf.RF-16.name: Core performance completed by general-purpose model priors rather than the neural signal
rf.RF-17.action: Require multi-day continuous in-hospital records and wear-stability data
rf.RF-17.name: Good in the lab, unstable in routine hospital use
rf.RF-18.action: Confirm the physical status and source of electrodes, chip, communication, power, algorithm and process one by one
rf.RF-18.name: A key element of the six-part stack is missing (no in-house electrode process, no power-management design, etc.)
rf.RF-19.action: Require the registration strategy document and the classification-determination application or consultation record
rf.RF-19.name: No clear regulatory pathway, or the product is being built purely as R&D
rf.RF-20.action: Require the full protocol, control design and follow-up table; verify the primary endpoint
rf.RF-20.name: Clinical data limited to case reports; no control arm, no follow-up
rf.RF-21.action: Require in-vivo duration and impedance-stability trend data from large-animal work
rf.RF-21.name: Technical breakthroughs discussed while bypassing safety and long-term stability
rf.RF-22.action: Verify reimbursement coding, provincial listing and the status of the billing-item application
rf.RF-22.name: Product is built but not sellable (no reimbursement code, no procurement pathway)
rf.RF-23.action: Compare type-test start date with design-freeze date and assess rework probability
rf.RF-23.name: Type testing started only after design freeze, forcing rework of the technical route
rf.RF-24.action: Require the payer, unit price, procurement decision chain and signed contracts
rf.RF-24.name: Cannot say who pays or how much; pitches only technical leadership
rf.RF-25.action: Check whether a replicable channel and a standardised sales process exist
rf.RF-25.name: Business plan depends on winning over a few key individuals rather than a repeatable channel
rf.RF-26.action: Verify transaction by transaction whether each partnership produced revenue or an accepted deliverable
rf.RF-26.name: Partnership count presented as commercial progress while no single scenario has closed
rf.RF-27.action: Split revenue by customer and channel and assess switching cost
rf.RF-27.name: Dependence on a single customer or channel exceeds half of revenue
rf.RF-28.action: Require the funding plan and signed term sheets; assess bridge feasibility
rf.RF-28.name: Runway below 6 months with no signed term sheet and no bridge arrangement
rf.RF-29.action: Require grant and related-party detail; recompute revenue after excluding them
rf.RF-29.name: Revenue mainly from grants and related parties; operating cash flow persistently negative
rf.RF-30.action: Request budget-versus-actual comparison and check approval of large expenditures
rf.RF-30.name: No budget control; spending unbudgeted after financing
rf.RF-31.action: Require the capitalisation policy and peer comparison; recompute profit on an expensed basis
rf.RF-31.name: R&D capitalisation ratio well above peers; profit flattered
rf.RF-32.action: Read the redemption triggers, obligor scope and liability cap line by line
rf.RF-32.name: Financing terms include a large redemption obligation or unlimited founder joint liability
rf.RF-33.action: Tick each channel's hard gates one by one and back-solve the conditions exit requires
rf.RF-33.name: Single exit path meeting no hard gate, yet priced as if exit were available
rf.RF-34.action: Model dilution and liquidation preference under flat and down-round scenarios
rf.RF-34.name: Follow-on round structure with clear downside/valuation-inversion risk
rf.RF-35.action: Check whether trigger metrics can coexist with the clinical cycle; push for milestone-based rewrite
rf.RF-35.name: VAM triggers tightly bound to short-term operating metrics, in conflict with a long-cycle sector
rf.RF-36.action: Run the equity and chain-of-title review; request all five node documents
rf.RF-36.name: Core patent ownership unclear, especially where university tech transfer has not completed valuation, approval and registration

rf.RF-37.name: Data collected without informed consent, or clinical data of non-compliant origin
rf.RF-38.action: Review guarantee documents and personal asset exposure; assess impact on decision-making
rf.RF-38.name: Founder carries personal joint liability
rf.RF-39.action: Request employment contracts, non-compete agreements and NDAs
rf.RF-39.name: No non-compete or confidentiality constraints on key personnel
rf.RF-40.action: Archive all marketing material and check it against the registered scope
rf.RF-40.name: Explicit efficacy claims in marketing, or production claims inconsistent with fact

rf.RF-43.action: Check the org chart and whether key positions are actually filled
rf.RF-43.name: Pure technical team, missing clinical, regulatory and sales roles

Where "real-time two-way interaction or closed-loop feedback" is not met, the product is regulated under the existing catalogue, the BCI device code no longer applies, and the platform-option narrative no longer applies either.

s.params.line1: - Parameter set: {id} | Baseline: built-in defaults v{ver} | Validation: {checks}
s.params.note: > This section documents the methodology parameters and their version used for this run. Parameters are methodological assumptions and do not constitute a valuation conclusion on any target.
s.rf.impact.dist: - The distribution of paths is not a severity ranking: five multi-multiple discounts add up to a lower price, one zero-out stops the deal. They cannot be summed and should not be compared on the same table.
s.rf.impact.gates: - **{n} zero-out item(s)**: once established, the valuation conclusion is void rather than discounted; multiple and probability discussion becomes moot.
s.rf.impact.note: > Severity answers "how bad"; the path answers "which line item it hits". They are orthogonal: a veto-level finding can land on deal terms while the asset itself is fine, and a watch-level IP defect zeroes the conclusion when the core patent sits outside the company.
s.rf.impact.th: | Path | What it discounts | Count | IDs |
s.rf.th: | ID | Dim | Finding | Severity | Status | Verification step |
s.runway.na: financials.cash or burn_monthly missing, runway cannot be computed
s.runway.th: | Cash and equivalents | Undrawn credit | Available liquidity | Monthly net burn | Runway (months) | Time to next milestone (months) | Ratio | Tier |
s.score.note: > Effective score = raw score × confidence discount (high {high} / medium {mid} / low {low}); weights have been adjusted by stage and gate factors and renormalised, with a per-dimension cap of {cap}.
s.score.th: | Dim | Name | Raw | Confidence | After discount | Effective weight | Contribution | Open checks |
s.score.topw: - Three heaviest dimensions: {list}. Stage factors explain why the same dimension carries different information value across rounds; gate factors explain how the asset-class determination corrects the basis.
s.val.exitGate: - **Exit hard gate not met**: the STAR Market Standard V requires an expected market capitalisation of at least RMB 4 billion, and a pharmaceutical or medical-device issuer must have at least one core product cleared to start Phase II; the current input is marked as not having that clearance.
s.val.exitNA: - **This path does not apply in this jurisdiction ({jd})**: {why}
s.val.impliedSuccess: - If the next milestone ({ms}) is discounted at the placeholder probability {prob}, the price implies a post-success value of {v}; check whether that falls within the comparable band.
s.val.inBand: - The implied multiple of {ps} sits at or below the band ceiling; no deviation flag triggered.
s.val.mismatch1: - **Basis mismatch**: measured against the determined family "{family}", implied P/S of {ps} already reaches {dev} the band ceiling ({cap}), and this asset class cannot support the multiple on technology narrative — only on revenue and profit.
s.val.mismatch2: - Against the declared class "{cls}" with a band ceiling of {cap}, the implied multiple is {dev}; that premium must be explained by a specific clinical milestone step-up, and the closed-loop and classification questions must be resolved first.
s.val.na: valuation.post_money and financials.revenue_ttm both missing, valuation basis cannot be checked
s.val.note: > This section checks the valuation basis; it is not a valuation conclusion. Multiple ranges are structural illustrations and must be calibrated to your own fund basis and comparables.
s.val.pendingRefuse: > Refused: revenue-multiple band edges for this jurisdiction ({jd}) are not verified (profile status=pending), so no band range, implied-multiple read or deviation warning is printed. Reason: a multiple without comparable samples is fabrication; the gap is listed in Chapter 7.
s.val.premium: - The premium must be explained by a milestone step-up: the implied multiple is currently {dev} the band ceiling.
s.val.psNA: Not applicable (no revenue or no revenue data)
s.val.sens.anchor: - **At a 24-month delay and a 12% discount rate, the same post-money requires post-success value to be {v} higher**; and those 24 months usually include another financing round, so dilution and discounting land in the same window and do not offset each other. This is the most commonly underweighted item in implantable device scheduling, and the reason this framework weights registration path at D4 (weight 0.16, the highest of the nine) rather than under commercial.
s.val.sens.delay: **2. Cost of delay.** A slipping milestone is not just later: the probability takes another discount while the discount period lengthens. The table gives the multiple by which post-success value must rise for the same post-money.
s.val.sens.note: > The two tables below answer only "what changed, and by how much". Every number is computed by the script with no manual adjustment. **The script gives the swing, not the comparable range** — whether the implied post-success value is reasonable must be checked against comparable transactions, and that step is not concluded here.
s.val.sens.prob: **1. Probability swing.** Base case assumes the next milestone ({ms}) succeeds at {base}, post-money {post}. For every 10 percentage points the success rate falls, the implied post-success value rises by base / (base − 0.10): the price did not change, the future simply became more valuable in the model.
s.val.sens.probTh: | Success assumption | Implied post-success value | vs base |
s.warn.none: - No anomaly to flag; the conclusion remains bounded by the completeness of input evidence.

verdict.preferred.desc: Above 85, milestone position no earlier than L4, and adequate runway
verdict.preferred.label: Preferred
verdict.veto.desc: A veto-level fatal red flag is open
verdict.veto.label: Reject
verdict.watch.desc: Effective weighted score below 55, or a fatal item with unknown status
verdict.watch.label: Watch
warn.aiRehab: asset.class=rehab_class2 with ai_based=true: under the 2026 No. 24 notice, AI-enabled stroke motor rehabilitation must be regulated as Class III; the Class II pathway needs review
warn.asOf: meta.as_of missing; the run date is used as the data cut-off
warn.burnMissing: financials.burn_monthly missing or non-positive: runway cannot be computed
warn.cashNegative: financials.cash is negative: cash and equivalents should not be negative; check the account basis
warn.classCodeMismatch: asset.classification_code={got} does not match the expected code for asset.class={cls} ({expect})
warn.classCodeMissing: asset.classification_code missing: under the 2026 No. 24 notice, {code} is the expected code; verify the classification determination
warn.classDomain: asset.class={v} is outside the allowed set; treated conservatively as "one-way monitoring (downgraded)"
warn.closedLoopMissing: asset.closed_loop missing: closed-loop status is unconfirmed; request the closed-loop link diagram
warn.companyName: company.name missing; output uses the placeholder "Unnamed entity"
warn.confDomain: Dimension {id} confidence={v} is outside the allowed set; treated as medium
warn.consumerClaim: asset.class=consumer_nondevice: a non-device may not claim to improve, restore or replace central nervous system function; external wording must match the regulatory status
warn.currency: meta.currency={v}: no FX conversion is supported, amounts are reported in their original currency, and cross-currency conclusions are not comparable
warn.dimEmpty: dimensions is empty: the nine-dimension score cannot be computed
warn.dimMissing: Dimensions not scored: {ids}; counted as 0 in the weighted total
warn.dimScoreMissing: Dimension {id} has no numeric score; treated as 0
warn.dimScoreRange: Dimension {id} score={score} is out of range; clamped to 0-100
warn.evidenceDate: Dimension {id} evidence item {n} has no date; comparability with the current conclusion is reduced
warn.evidenceSource: Dimension {id} evidence item {n} has no source and is not traceable
warn.grant: Grants account for {v}% of revenue: operating revenue quality must be assessed separately after excluding them
warn.grossMargin: Gross margin {v}% is below 30%: explain whether the hardware mix includes low-margin integration or project revenue
warn.mismatch: Valuation basis mismatch: against the determined family "{family}", implied P/S of {ps} is {dev} the band ceiling ({cap}), and the option method does not apply to this asset class
warn.modalityMissing: asset.modality missing: modality unconfirmed, which affects the technical dimensions and the regulatory pathway
warn.msEmpty: milestones.items is empty: milestone position cannot be established; runway and valuation checks degrade
warn.msEvidence: Milestone {id} is marked done but evidence is incomplete ({got}/{total}); missing: {lack}
warn.msNoDate: Milestone {id} is marked done but has no completion date, so it cannot be verified
warn.msOffPath: Milestone(s) {ids} are not on the typical path for this asset class; confirm the path determination
warn.openLoop: asset.closed_loop=false: the classification determination requires all four core characteristics, and "real-time two-way interaction or closed-loop feedback" is not met; the asset is downgraded from "{from}" to "{to}" and the option method no longer applies
warn.rdRatio: R&D expense ratio {v}% is high: explain the fit with revenue scale and dependence on further financing
warn.rfStatus: Red flag {id} status={v} is outside the allowed set; treated as unknown
warn.rfUnknown: Red-flag ID {id} does not exist in RF_LIBRARY (RF-01 to RF-44); ignored
warn.runwayFloor: Runway of {v} months is below the {floor}-month floor (cash and undrawn credit only; payables extension excluded)
warn.schemaVersion: Input schema_version={v} is not compatible with script {cur} (different major version, or higher minor version); unrecognised fields will be ignored
warn.snr: asset.snr_db={v} dB combined with semantic or intent decoding claims: high-accuracy semantic decoding is not physically plausible at this SNR; require the control result with EMG / EOG channels disabled
warn.stageDomain: company.stage={v} is outside the allowed set; weights are computed as if stage a
